title: Fsfnet fantasy-science fiction fanzine
summary: FSFnet was an electronic fanzine for fantasy and science fiction fans, distributed over BITNET in the mid-1980s and edited by 'Orny' Liscomb. The issues gathered by this record include short reviews, featured-author profiles, letters of comment, and original fiction and verse from readers on various university networks. Reviews discuss the 1984 film Dune and Diana Paxson's novel Brisingamen. Featured-author pieces cover M.A.R. Barker's Tekumel setting, with its roleplaying games and the novel Man of Gold, and Larry Niven's Known Space and Ringworld books. The fiction includes a short tale of an errant knight in a frozen kingdom, a close-encounter story set on a cold night patrol, and the opening chapters of a heist story about a thief infiltrating a bardic college. Other pieces include a serialized chronicle of a lost empire with translated sources and footnotes, an Orwellian poem, and a fiction excerpt about a wedding and a father's test of a suitor. The editorial material solicits submissions and announces play-by-net Diplomacy games and dungeon modules, giving a picture of early computer-network fandom.
